task_9.title: Restore TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication without certificate verification
task_9.description: urllib3 2.2.0 restores TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication for SSL contexts created when server certificate validation is disabled. This allows conditional client certificate authentication to continue working in environments that intentionally use non-verifying certificate requirements, while preserving compatibility with SSL context implementations that do not expose post-handshake authentication support.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that TLS 1.3 post-handshake client certificate authentication remains available when urllib3 creates an SSL context with server certificate validation disabled.

expectation.grounded: urllib3.util.ssl_.create_urllib3_context should enable SSLContext.post_handshake_auth whenever that public SSLContext attribute is present and not None, regardless of whether cert_reqs is unspecified, ssl.CERT_NONE, ssl.CERT_OPTIONAL, or ssl.CERT_REQUIRED. Contexts where post_handshake_auth is absent or None must continue to be accepted without raising an error due to that capability check.
expectation.conceptual: A caller that disables server certificate verification should still be able to connect to TLS 1.3 services that request a client certificate after the initial handshake. Unsupported SSL context implementations should continue to behave gracefully.

constraints.grounded: Enabling TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication must not depend on cert_reqs being ssl.CERT_REQUIRED. The behavior must remain guarded by SSLContext.post_handshake_auth availability so OpenSSL or pyOpenSSL-backed contexts without usable support are not forced into an unsupported state.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should restore client-certificate authentication compatibility without broadening assumptions about SSL backends or changing unrelated certificate verification behavior.

behavior: create_urllib3_context sets post_handshake_auth to True on SSL contexts that expose a non-None post_handshake_auth attribute.
post_handshake_auth is enabled independently of the selected server certificate requirement mode, including non-verifying modes.
TLS 1.3 connections that rely on conditional client certificate authentication can respond to post-handshake certificate requests even when server certificate validation is disabled.
SSL contexts without a usable post_handshake_auth attribute continue through context creation without an attribute-related failure.
acceptance_criteria: Given an SSL context with post_handshake_auth available, when create_urllib3_context is called with server certificate verification disabled, then post_handshake_auth should be enabled on the returned context.
Given an SSL context with post_handshake_auth available, when create_urllib3_context is called with any supported cert_reqs setting, then TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication should remain enabled.
Given an SSL context where post_handshake_auth is unavailable or None, when create_urllib3_context is called, then context creation should complete without requiring that capability.

When connecting to a TLS 1.3 service that performs conditional client certificate authentication after the handshake, disabling server certificate validation should not prevent the client from participating in post-handshake authentication.

task_7.title: Correct HTTPS proxy verification reporting
task_7.description: urllib3 2.2.0 corrects connection verification metadata for requests that use an HTTPS proxy, especially when the proxy forwards to an HTTP target. The target verification state is no longer reported as verified merely because the TLS connection to the proxy was verified, and proxy verification is tracked separately so warning behavior can distinguish the two.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTPS proxy connections report proxy TLS verification and target TLS verification independently, so an HTTPS proxy forwarding to an HTTP target does not cause the target-facing HTTPSConnection.is_verified state to appear verified.

expectation.grounded: For HTTPSConnection instances using a forwarding proxy, HTTPSConnection.is_verified must be false because the target endpoint itself is not TLS-verified through a CONNECT tunnel. When a proxy connection has been established and HTTPSConnection.proxy_is_verified has not already been recorded, proxy_is_verified must reflect the TLS verification result for the proxy connection. Non-forwarding direct or tunneled HTTPS target connections must continue to report is_verified from the target TLS verification result. HTTPConnection.proxy_is_forwarding should identify the case where a proxy is configured without a tunnel. HTTPSConnectionPool must consider both is_verified and proxy_is_verified before emitting an unverified HTTPS warning.
expectation.conceptual: A secure proxy being verified must not be treated as proof that the destination server was verified. Applications should be able to tell whether the proxy was trusted, whether the destination was trusted, and whether a warning is warranted based on those separate facts.

constraints.grounded: Do not set HTTPSConnection.is_verified to true solely from a verified HTTPS proxy when the proxy is forwarding instead of tunneling. Do not overwrite an existing proxy_is_verified value that was already established for a tunnel. Preserve existing verification semantics for direct HTTPS requests and CONNECT-tunneled HTTPS targets. Preserve unverified HTTPS warnings when neither the target verification state nor the proxy verification state is true.
constraints.conceptual: Keep request routing and successful responses unchanged while making the exposed security state accurate. Avoid noisy warnings for a verified secure proxy, but continue to surface genuinely unverified secure connections.

behavior: An HTTPS proxy forwarding to an HTTP target reports the target verification state as false even when the proxy TLS certificate was verified.
A verified HTTPS proxy connection records the proxy verification state separately from the target verification state.
Forwarding proxy detection is exposed through proxy_is_forwarding when a proxy is configured and no tunnel is in use.
Direct HTTPS connections and tunneled HTTPS target connections continue to report target verification based on the target TLS handshake.
Unverified HTTPS warnings are emitted only when both the target verification state and proxy verification state are not verified.
acceptance_criteria: Given a trusted HTTPS proxy forwarding a request to an HTTP target, when the request completes, the connection should report is_verified as false and proxy_is_verified as true.

Given a trusted HTTPS proxy tunneling to an HTTPS target with a valid certificate, when the request completes, the target verification state should remain true and the proxy verification state should remain true.
Given a direct HTTPS request or a tunneled HTTPS target request, when target certificate verification succeeds, the connection should continue to report the target as verified.
When a proxied HTTPS connection has an already recorded proxy verification state, later connection handling should not replace that recorded proxy verification state.
When neither the target nor proxy TLS verification state is verified for an HTTPS connection, an unverified HTTPS warning should still be emitted.

When only the target state is unverified because an HTTPS proxy is forwarding to an HTTP target but the proxy TLS state is verified, an unverified HTTPS warning should not be emitted solely for that forwarding arrangement.

task_3.title: Add rudimentary HTTP/2 support
task_3.description: Version 2.2.0 adds an explicitly enabled HTTP/2 transport path for simple HTTPS requests. The new support can switch urllib3's HTTPS connection handling to an HTTP/2 connection class, negotiate h2 via ALPN, and return a buffered HTTP/2 response. The initial scope is intentionally limited and does not cover multiplexing, connection reuse, request bodies, streaming responses, or proxies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Provide rudimentary opt-in HTTP/2 support for HTTPS requests while preserving the ability to restore the existing HTTP/1.1 HTTPS behavior and clearly rejecting unsupported HTTP/2 scenarios.

expectation.grounded: The urllib3.http2 module should expose HTTP2Connection, HTTP2Response, inject_into_urllib3(), and extract_from_urllib3(). Calling inject_into_urllib3() should make new HTTPSConnectionPool usage rely on HTTP2Connection and advertise h2 via ALPN. HTTP2Connection should initiate the HTTP/2 client connection after TLS, create a single stream for each request, send the required HTTPS HTTP/2 pseudo-header fields and lowercased request headers, read the full response body before returning, acknowledge received flow-controlled data, close after each response, and return HTTP2Response with status, headers, request URL, version 20, and bytes data. Calling extract_from_urllib3() should restore the original HTTPSConnection behavior and HTTP/1.1 ALPN advertisement.
expectation.conceptual: Users can opt into simple HTTP/2 over HTTPS for requests that do not need request bodies, proxying, streaming, multiplexing, redirects, or connection reuse. Responses should be fully buffered and presented through urllib3 response semantics with the correct protocol version, status, headers, and body. Users can opt back out to normal HTTPS behavior.

constraints.grounded: HTTP/2 support must remain opt-in through urllib3.http2 injection and must be reversible through extraction. HTTP2Connection should reject proxy configuration and non-empty request data with NotImplementedError, ignore empty send operations, close and reset HTTP/2 state after each response, and avoid claiming support for multiplexing, connection reuse, request bodies, response streaming, or proxies. The default HTTPS behavior should remain HTTP/1.1 when HTTP/2 has not been injected or after extraction.
constraints.conceptual: Do not present this as complete HTTP/2 support. Unsupported features should either remain unavailable or fail explicitly, and enabling HTTP/2 should not permanently alter HTTPS behavior once the user opts back out.

behavior: A new urllib3.http2 module provides HTTP2Connection, HTTP2Response, inject_into_urllib3(), and extract_from_urllib3().
inject_into_urllib3() switches urllib3 HTTPS connection creation to HTTP2Connection and advertises h2 via ALPN; extract_from_urllib3() restores the original HTTPS connection class and HTTP/1.1 ALPN.
HTTP2Connection.connect() performs normal HTTPS setup, initiates the HTTP/2 client connection, and sends the initial HTTP/2 connection data.
HTTP2Connection.putrequest() creates a new HTTP/2 stream and records HTTPS request metadata as HTTP/2 pseudo-header fields, including bracketed host formatting for IPv6 authorities.
HTTP2Connection.putheader() records outgoing headers with lowercased header names for HTTP/2 transmission.
HTTP2Connection.endheaders() sends the accumulated headers and ends the request stream, so no request body is sent.
HTTP2Connection.send() ignores empty payloads and raises NotImplementedError for non-empty request body data.

HTTP2Connection.getresponse() reads until stream completion, ignores informational responses, parses the final status and headers, buffers all data frames, acknowledges received flow-controlled data, closes the connection, and returns an HTTP2Response.
HTTP2Response exposes the buffered data, status, headers, request URL, HTTP/2 version indicator, no reason phrase, zero remaining length, and no redirect location.
HTTP2Connection rejects proxy configuration and resets its HTTP/2 state when closed, leaving multiplexing and connection reuse unsupported.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls urllib3.http2.inject_into_urllib3(), subsequent HTTPSConnectionPool connections should use HTTP2Connection and advertise h2 via ALPN.

Given an HTTPS server that speaks HTTP/2, when a simple GET without a request body is sent after injection, it should return an HTTP2Response containing the final status, response headers, request URL, full response bytes, and HTTP/2 version indicator.
When response data frames are received, the client should buffer their bytes into the response data and acknowledge the received flow-controlled data before completing the response.
When informational HTTP/2 response events are received before the final response headers, they should not prevent the final response from being returned.
When non-empty request body data is sent through HTTP2Connection, it should raise NotImplementedError; when the send payload is empty, it should complete without error.
When HTTP/2 connection construction receives proxy configuration, it should raise NotImplementedError.
When an HTTP/2 response completes or the connection is closed, the connection should close the underlying transport and reset its HTTP/2 stream/header state rather than reusing the connection.
When urllib3.http2.extract_from_urllib3() is called after injection, new HTTPS connections should return to the original HTTPSConnection behavior and advertise HTTP/1.1 through ALPN.

task_6.title: Preserve caller headers during JSON and proxy requests
task_6.description: urllib3 2.2.0 fixes request header handling so caller-provided header mappings are not modified when a JSON request needs a default Content-Type, while preserving the outgoing request behavior. The same defensive header-copying behavior is applied before proxy headers are merged for non-tunneled proxy requests.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that request APIs do not mutate caller-provided headers when preparing JSON request bodies or merging proxy headers, while still sending the appropriate headers on the wire.

expectation.grounded: When RequestMethods.request or higher-level urllib3 request helpers are called with json= and a headers mapping, the original headers object must remain unchanged. If the mapping lacks Content-Type, the outgoing request should still include application/json. Header name checks for an existing Content-Type must remain case-insensitive. In HTTPConnectionPool request handling, proxy headers must be included for non-tunneled proxy requests without mutating the supplied headers mapping.
expectation.conceptual: Supplying headers to a request should be side-effect free. urllib3 may add default JSON or proxy-related headers to the request it sends, but those additions must not alter the caller's original header data. Existing user-specified content types must continue to be respected.

constraints.grounded: Do not change JSON body serialization semantics, the default application/json behavior for json= requests without an explicit Content-Type, or case-insensitive Content-Type detection. Do not require headers mappings to support item assignment when urllib3 adds the default JSON Content-Type. Preserve proxy header behavior for the actual request while preventing mutation of the input headers mapping.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must avoid new side effects without changing the request that users intended to send. Immutable or reused header mappings should be accepted wherever they were otherwise valid.

behavior: A json= request with caller-provided headers that omit Content-Type sends a JSON Content-Type on the outgoing request without adding that key to the caller's headers object.
A json= request with caller-provided Content-Type, regardless of header-name casing, preserves that content type and does not add or overwrite it.
A json= request can be prepared with a headers mapping that should not be mutated in place, including mappings that do not allow assignment, as long as the mapping can be read as headers.
When proxy headers are applied for a non-tunneled proxy request, they are present on the outgoing request while the original request headers are not changed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a request made with json= and a headers mapping that lacks Content-Type, when the request is prepared and sent, then the outgoing request includes application/json and the original headers mapping is unchanged.

Given a request made with json= and a headers mapping that already contains Content-Type using any casing, when the request is prepared and sent, then urllib3 preserves that content type and leaves the original mapping unchanged.
Given a readable but non-assignable headers mapping on a json= request, when urllib3 needs to add the default JSON Content-Type, then request preparation succeeds without mutating that mapping.

Given a non-tunneled proxy request with existing request headers, when proxy headers are merged, then the outgoing request contains the proxy headers but the original request headers object remains unchanged.

task_10.title: Separate integration validation workflow
task_10.description: The 2.2.0 update adds distributor-facing guidance that long-running integration validation is separated from the default validation flow and must be invoked through an explicit integration mode. No production library code changes are present in the provided code diff, so there is no observable runtime API change for urllib3 users.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that downstream distributors can distinguish the default validation workflow from the slower integration validation workflow introduced in 2.2.0, without implying any change to urllib3 runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: The release note must communicate that downstream distributors need an additional pytest invocation using the public --integration option to cover integration-only checks. The provided production code diff is empty, so no public urllib3 APIs, classes, functions, exceptions, warnings, return values, or runtime states should be described as changed.
expectation.conceptual: Package maintainers should understand that the release changes how the project expects optional long-running validation to be selected, while regular library behavior remains unchanged for application users.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce or describe runtime behavior changes for HTTPSConnectionPool, HTTPResponse, SSL handling, or any other urllib3 public API based on this update. Do not frame the release as requiring application code changes.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be treated as distributor and maintainer guidance only, with no compatibility impact for normal urllib3 consumers.

behavior: No production library behavior change is evidenced by the provided code diff.
The release note exposes a distributor-facing distinction between default validation and an explicit integration validation mode.
Long-running integration validation is documented as opt-in rather than part of the default validation path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a downstream distributor is upgrading to 2.2.0, when they read the release information, then they should be able to identify that integration validation is separate from the default validation workflow.

Given an application depends on urllib3 runtime APIs, when it upgrades from 2.1.0 to 2.2.0 for this change, then it should not need code changes for request, response, SSL, warning, or exception behavior.
Given the provided production diff contains no library changes, when documenting the upgrade impact, then the stated impact should remain limited to distributor-facing validation workflow guidance.

task_2.title: Add HTTPResponse.read1 support
task_2.description: urllib3 2.2.0 adds a read1-style streaming API to HTTPResponse so callers can consume response bodies using the one-buffer read semantics exposed by Python HTTP and buffered IO objects, while retaining urllib3 content decoding and connection state behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTPResponse supports read1-style body consumption for streamed responses, including optional content decoding and consistent end-of-stream handling.

expectation.grounded: BaseHTTPResponse and HTTPResponse should expose read1(amt=None, decode_content=None). HTTPResponse.read1() should use the underlying response object's read1 behavior, return bytes, honor amt including amt=0, default decode_content to the response's configured decode_content setting, decode supported content encodings when requested, and buffer decoded bytes so later read1 calls can return already-decoded data before reading more raw data. Once decoded content has been read through read1, a later read1 call that disables decoding should raise RuntimeError. Premature EOF should continue to surface as IncompleteRead when applicable, and EOF should close the wrapped response consistently, including when the known remaining length has been consumed.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read streamed HTTP responses one buffered chunk at a time through HTTPResponse.read1(), with the same decoding controls and error behavior they expect from existing response reads.

constraints.grounded: Existing HTTPResponse.read(), stream(), preload_content, decode_content defaults, Content-Length accounting, decoder error propagation, and large SSL response handling must not regress. read1(None) may return a partial chunk rather than draining the entire response, while read1(0) must be a no-op that returns empty bytes without consuming data.
constraints.conceptual: The new read1 API must be additive and must not change existing response-reading behavior for callers that continue using the established APIs.

behavior: HTTPResponse instances provide a read1 method accepting an optional byte amount and optional decode_content flag.
Calling read1 with amt=0 returns empty bytes without attempting to consume response body data.
Calling read1 with no amount delegates to one-buffer read semantics and can return less than the full remaining response body.
When decoding is disabled, read1 returns raw response bytes.
When decoding is enabled or inherited from the response default, read1 decodes supported Content-Encoding values before returning data.
Decoded output that exceeds the requested amount is retained and returned by subsequent read1 calls before more raw bytes are read.
If a decoder needs more raw input before producing output, read1 continues reading raw chunks until decoded bytes are available or EOF is reached.
After decoded content has been consumed through read1, attempting to call read1 with decode_content=False raises RuntimeError.
When read1 reaches EOF, or consumes the known remaining response length, the wrapped response file is closed consistently.
When read1 encounters premature EOF while a nonzero content length remains, IncompleteRead is raised under the same conditions as existing raw reads.
Very large SSL response reads remain bounded so read1 does not request more than the platform-safe maximum from the underlying response object in a single operation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a streamed HTTPResponse, when a caller invokes read1(1), read1(2), and then read1() on a plain body, it should return the body in successive byte chunks and eventually return empty bytes at EOF.
Given a streamed HTTPResponse with content decoding enabled and a supported compressed body, when a caller consumes it with read1, it should return decoded body bytes rather than encoded wire bytes.
Given read1(0), when the response still has unread data, it should return empty bytes without consuming body data or closing the response.
Given decoded bytes are buffered from a previous read1 call, when read1 is called again, it should return buffered decoded bytes before reading additional raw data.
Given read1 has already returned decoded content, when a caller later calls read1 with decoding disabled, it should raise RuntimeError.
Given a response with a known remaining length, when read1 consumes the final byte, it should close the wrapped response stream.
Given a response with an unknown remaining length, when read1 reads until the underlying stream returns EOF, it should close the wrapped response stream.
Given a response body ends before the declared remaining length is satisfied, when read1 performs a nonzero read, it should raise IncompleteRead.
Given a very large SSL response, when read1 is used to consume it, it should continue to return data in bounded chunks without overflowing platform read limits.

task_8.title: Handle OpenSSL 3.2 proxy TLS mismatch errors
task_8.description: urllib3 now recognizes the OpenSSL 3.2.0 error surface produced when an HTTP-only proxy is mistakenly configured with an HTTPS proxy URL, so users receive the existing clear proxy misconfiguration diagnostic instead of an opaque SSL failure. Request handling also tolerates a connection-reset errno in the same platform-specific path that already handled protocol errno conditions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTP-only proxies mistakenly configured as HTTPS are diagnosed consistently under OpenSSL 3.2.0, and ensure expected platform connection-reset signals in request handling do not cause unnecessary failures.

expectation.grounded: When an HTTPS-declared proxy connection fails with OpenSSL 3.2.0's record-layer failure condition, urllib3 should wrap the failure as a ProxyError with the same HTTP-only proxy guidance already used for recognized TLS protocol/version mismatch failures. The original SSL failure should remain attached as the underlying cause. HTTPConnectionPool request handling should treat errno.ECONNRESET like errno.EPROTOTYPE in the already-handled OSError path, while preserving propagation for other OSError values.
expectation.conceptual: Users who accidentally configure an HTTP proxy as HTTPS should get a clear configuration error instead of an unclear SSL failure, including on newer OpenSSL versions. Connection-pool handling should remain resilient to known platform-level reset signals without hiding unrelated network errors.

constraints.grounded: Apply the HTTP-only proxy diagnostic only for an HTTPS proxy scheme and recognized proxy TLS/protocol mismatch failures, including the OpenSSL 3.2.0 record-layer failure condition. Do not change handling for unrelated proxy failures, non-HTTPS proxy schemes, OSError errno values other than EPROTOTYPE and ECONNRESET in this path, BrokenPipeError behavior, timeout handling, retries, or response decoding.
constraints.conceptual: Do not mask unrelated SSL, proxy, or socket failures, and do not change behavior for correctly configured proxies or ordinary response processing. The compatibility fix should be limited to the newly observed OpenSSL/platform error surfaces.

behavior: An OpenSSL 3.2.0 record-layer failure while connecting through an HTTPS-declared proxy is classified as a likely HTTP-only proxy misconfiguration.
The resulting ProxyError includes the established user-facing guidance for HTTP proxy configured as HTTPS and retains the original SSL exception as the cause.
Previously recognized TLS/protocol mismatch failures for the same proxy misconfiguration continue to receive the same diagnostic treatment.
ProxyError wrapping for non-HTTPS proxy schemes and unrecognized SSL failures remains unchanged.
HTTPConnectionPool no longer fails immediately solely because the handled request path raises OSError with errno.ECONNRESET; it proceeds as it already did for errno.EPROTOTYPE.
Unexpected OSError errno values in that request-handling path continue to propagate.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HTTP-only proxy is configured with an HTTPS proxy URL and OpenSSL 3.2.0 reports its record-layer failure condition during proxy TLS negotiation, when a request is made through urllib3 proxy handling, it should raise ProxyError with clear HTTP-vs-HTTPS proxy misconfiguration guidance.

Given the same proxy-wrapping path is reached for a proxy scheme other than HTTPS, when the underlying failure matches that record-layer condition, it should not add the HTTPS-proxy-specific diagnostic.

Given proxy TLS failures that match the previously recognized protocol/version mismatch conditions, when connection through an HTTPS-declared proxy fails, the existing HTTP-only proxy diagnostic should still be produced.
Given HTTPConnectionPool encounters OSError with errno.ECONNRESET in the handled request path, when response processing can continue, it should not fail solely because of that errno.
Given HTTPConnectionPool encounters an OSError with any other unexpected errno in that same path, when the error is handled, it should still be raised to the caller.

task_5.title: Normalize proxy verification state
task_5.description: The 2.2.0 update fixes proxy connection verification metadata so applications can rely on explicit boolean verification states after proxied HTTP and HTTPS connections. It also keeps destination verification from being overstated when a forwarding proxy is responsible for upstream verification, and normalizes the TLS server hostname used for HTTPS connections with trailing-dot hostnames.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that proxied HTTP and HTTPS connections expose deterministic and truthful verification state after connecting, with proxy verification and destination verification reported separately.

expectation.grounded: After HTTPConnection or HTTPSConnection connects through a proxy, proxy_is_verified must be a boolean rather than None. Plain or otherwise unverified proxy paths should report False, HTTPS proxy paths should report the actual TLS verification result for the proxy, and an established HTTPS proxy verification result must not be overwritten while completing the destination connection. HTTPSConnection.is_verified must only report successful destination verification when the client verifies the destination directly; forwarding proxy connections should not report the destination as verified by the client. HTTPS TLS validation should use a normalized server hostname when the requested hostname has a trailing dot.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to inspect a completed proxied connection and always get clear true-or-false answers for whether the proxy was verified and whether the destination was verified. These states should reflect what the client actually verified, including proxy forwarding scenarios and hostnames written with a trailing dot.

constraints.grounded: Do not change whether otherwise valid proxied requests succeed. Keep proxy_is_verified distinct from HTTPSConnection.is_verified. Do not treat an unencrypted or unverified proxy connection as verified. Do not report a forwarding proxy's upstream verification as direct client verification of the destination. Preserve an already determined HTTPS proxy verification result while completing the destination connection.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain request compatibility while making verification reporting explicit, conservative, and separated between the proxy and the final destination.

behavior: Connections through a proxy no longer leave proxy_is_verified as None after the proxy connection is established.
Proxy paths without TLS-verified proxy identity expose proxy_is_verified as False.
An HTTPSConnection that tunnels through an HTTP proxy sets proxy_is_verified to False after establishing the proxy connection.
Proxy paths that verify an HTTPS proxy keep proxy_is_verified aligned with the TLS verification result for the proxy.
If an HTTPSConnection completes through a proxy and proxy_is_verified has not already been set by tunnel setup, it is set from the TLS verification result available for the proxied connection.
For HTTPS forwarding proxy connections, HTTPSConnection.is_verified is False because the client has not directly verified the destination server.
For direct or tunneled HTTPS destination connections, HTTPSConnection.is_verified continues to reflect the TLS verification result for the destination.
HTTPS connections use the trailing-dot-normalized hostname for TLS server hostname validation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connection through a proxy, when the connection completes, proxy_is_verified should be a boolean rather than None.
Given a connection through a plain or otherwise unverified proxy path, when the proxy connection completes, proxy_is_verified should be False.
Given an HTTPSConnection tunneling through an HTTP proxy, when the tunnel is established and the connection completes, proxy_is_verified should be False rather than None.
Given a connection through an HTTPS proxy, when the TLS connection to the proxy is verified, proxy_is_verified should be True; when it is not verified, proxy_is_verified should be False.
Given an HTTPS proxy tunnel where proxy verification has already been determined, when destination TLS setup completes, the proxy verification value should remain unchanged.
Given an HTTPS request through a forwarding proxy, when the connection completes, is_verified should not indicate direct client verification of the destination.
Given a directly verified or tunneled HTTPS destination, when the connection completes, is_verified should continue to reflect the destination TLS verification result.

Given an HTTPS hostname supplied with a trailing dot, when TLS validation occurs, the effective server hostname should be normalized so verification behavior matches the same hostname without the trailing dot.

task_4.title: Fix HTTPS proxy handling for trailing-dot hostnames
task_4.description: HTTPS requests made through proxies should handle fully qualified domain names with trailing dots the same way direct HTTPS connections do, avoiding certificate hostname validation failures caused only by the trailing dot. The connection verification state should also accurately distinguish target verification from proxy verification when forwarding proxies are involved.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that proxied HTTPS requests to hostnames ending in a trailing dot do not fail SSL certificate validation solely because the requested URL uses a fully qualified domain form.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3 establishes an HTTPS connection through ProxyManager or related proxy connection flows, the server hostname used for TLS wrapping and certificate hostname matching should ignore trailing dots from fully qualified domain names. Requests such as an HTTPS origin whose certificate is issued for the non-trailing-dot hostname should no longer raise SSL-related retry failures only because the request URL host ends with a dot. HTTPSConnection.is_verified should represent whether the target was verified, and HTTPSConnection.proxy_is_verified should represent whether the proxy TLS connection was verified when that state is available.
expectation.conceptual: A user should be able to access a valid HTTPS site through a proxy whether the hostname is written with or without a final dot, while still receiving accurate security status about what endpoint was actually verified.

constraints.grounded: Do not weaken certificate validation for direct HTTPS connections, CONNECT-tunneled proxy connections, explicit assert_hostname values, or fingerprint checks. Forwarding proxy connections must not report the target endpoint as verified by urllib3 when the proxy is the party performing target verification. Existing proxy verification state must not be overwritten after it has already been established during tunnel setup.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must remove only the false hostname mismatch caused by fully qualified domain spelling and must preserve strict TLS verification and truthful verification reporting for all proxy modes.

behavior: Trailing dots are removed from the hostname used for TLS server-name handling and certificate hostname matching.
Proxied HTTPS requests to otherwise valid hosts with trailing-dot fully qualified domain names no longer fail with SSL hostname mismatch or retry errors solely due to the trailing dot.
The same host requested without a trailing dot retains its existing HTTPS proxy behavior.
For forwarding proxy connections, the target connection verification flag is reported as false because urllib3 has not verified the target certificate directly.
When a proxy connection has been established and proxy verification has not already been recorded, the proxy verification flag is populated from the TLS verification result for that proxy connection.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proxied HTTPS request to a hostname ending in a dot whose certificate is valid for the same hostname without the dot, when the request is made, then it should complete without failing certificate hostname validation solely because of the trailing dot.
Given a proxied HTTPS request to the same hostname without a trailing dot, when the request is made, then its existing success and verification behavior should be unchanged.
When urllib3 reports verification state for a forwarding proxy connection, it should not claim the target HTTPS endpoint was verified by urllib3.
When urllib3 has verification information for the proxy TLS connection and no proxy verification state has already been set, it should expose that state through the proxy verification indicator.
When direct HTTPS, CONNECT-tunneled HTTPS, assert-hostname, or fingerprint verification paths are used, they should continue enforcing their normal certificate validation rules.

task_1.title: Support urllib3 in Emscripten and Pyodide
task_1.description: urllib3 2.2.0 adds browser/WASM runtime support for Emscripten and Pyodide by routing HTTP and HTTPS requests through browser APIs. Standard urllib3 request APIs should work in these environments, with streaming responses available in cross-origin isolated worker contexts where threading and a streaming worker are ready, and buffered browser requests used as a fallback otherwise.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 can perform HTTP and HTTPS requests from Emscripten/Pyodide browser runtimes using the standard urllib3 APIs, including incremental response streaming when the browser environment supports it.

expectation.grounded: When running on the Emscripten platform, importing urllib3 should install EmscriptenHTTPConnection and EmscriptenHTTPSConnection for HTTPConnectionPool, HTTPSConnectionPool, urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection, and urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection. These connections should accept the existing request/getresponse calling pattern, support absolute URLs and path-only URLs, send the request method, headers, body, timeout, and decode-content preference through browser-backed transport, and return a BaseHTTPResponse-compatible object with status, headers, url, connection, retries, data, read, stream, read_chunked, json, release_conn, drain_conn, and close behavior. With preload_content disabled, a cross-origin isolated, non-main-browser-thread environment with Worker and Blob support and a ready streaming worker should use fetch-backed streaming; otherwise the request should fall back to a buffered XMLHttpRequest path and surface a single relevant browser-console warning. Timeout failures should be exposed as urllib3.exceptions.TimeoutError, while non-timeout browser request failures should be exposed as http.client.HTTPException.
expectation.conceptual: Users running urllib3 in Pyodide, PyScript, or other Emscripten browser environments should be able to make HTTP and HTTPS requests through familiar urllib3 interfaces. Capable browser worker environments should deliver streamed response bodies incrementally, while unsupported environments should still complete requests through buffered browser APIs and report limitations through warnings and standard Python exceptions.

constraints.grounded: Do not change urllib3 behavior on non-Emscripten platforms. Preserve connection-pool compatibility for connection implementations that do not expose a normal HTTP version string. In Emscripten transports, browser-managed features such as proxy tunneling, socket options, source addresses, and custom certificate verification should not be required to make requests. Headers that would trigger unintended CORS behavior, including User-Agent, should be omitted by the browser transport. Low-level JavaScript exceptions must not leak through the high-level urllib3 response API.
constraints.conceptual: The new browser runtime support should integrate without disrupting existing urllib3 users, should degrade gracefully when streaming or timeout features are unavailable, and should keep browser-specific limitations behind the normal urllib3 API contract.

behavior: On the Emscripten platform, urllib3 automatically switches HTTP and HTTPS pools and connection classes to browser-backed Emscripten connection implementations.

Emscripten HTTP and HTTPS connections accept standard request parameters, normalize path-only request targets against the connection scheme, host, and port, and provide responses through getresponse().
Requests carry method, body, headers, timeout, and decode-content intent into the browser-backed transport, while CORS-sensitive ignored headers are not sent.
When preload_content is false and streaming prerequisites are satisfied, responses are read through a fetch-backed stream using a browser worker and shared buffer.
When streaming is unavailable, not ready, or not permitted by the browser context, requests fall back to a buffered XMLHttpRequest transport and emit a warning only once for that limitation.
On the browser main thread, requests use synchronous XMLHttpRequest and warn once when a timeout is configured because browser main-thread timeouts cannot be enforced by this transport.
In worker contexts, buffered XMLHttpRequest responses are handled as binary array buffers and configured timeouts are applied.
The Emscripten response wrapper exposes BaseHTTPResponse-compatible status, headers, URL, connection, retry metadata, body reading, streaming, JSON parsing, and connection release behavior.
Reading a response to completion or closing it releases or closes the associated connection consistently with urllib3 pool expectations.

Timeout failures are converted to urllib3.exceptions.TimeoutError, other browser request failures are converted to http.client.HTTPException, and getresponse() without a pending response raises ResponseNotReady.
streaming_ready() and wait_for_streaming_ready() expose whether the streaming fetch worker is available and ready for use.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python is running on the Emscripten platform, when urllib3 is imported, then standard urllib3 HTTP and HTTPS connection pools and connection classes should use browser-backed Emscripten implementations without requiring user opt-in.

When a user sends an HTTP or HTTPS request through PoolManager, HTTPConnectionPool, HTTPSConnectionPool, HTTPConnection, or HTTPSConnection in Pyodide, it should return a BaseHTTPResponse-compatible response with observable status, headers, URL, connection, and body accessors.
When a request target is path-only, it should be resolved against the connection scheme, host, and port before being sent through the browser transport.
When a request includes method, headers, and body data, the browser transport should send those values except for headers intentionally suppressed to avoid unintended CORS behavior.

Given preload_content is disabled and the runtime is cross-origin isolated, running outside the browser main thread, has Worker and Blob support, and the streaming worker is ready, reading or iterating the response should deliver streamed body data incrementally.

Given streaming prerequisites are absent or the streaming worker is not ready, the same request should still complete through buffered XMLHttpRequest and should emit only one warning for the streaming limitation.

Given a timeout is configured on the browser main thread, the request should still be attempted and should warn that the timeout limitation applies; given a timeout occurs in a worker-backed request, callers should receive urllib3.exceptions.TimeoutError.
When browser fetch or XMLHttpRequest reports a non-timeout request failure, callers should receive http.client.HTTPException rather than a JavaScript-specific exception.
When a response body is fully consumed or the response is closed, the associated connection should be released or closed according to urllib3 pool semantics.
On non-Emscripten platforms, importing urllib3 should leave the existing connection classes and runtime behavior unchanged.
